text: Chapter 7 teaches extended block chord vocabulary for the II/V/I progression by combining triads, tetrads, quartal chords, inversions, and tritone substitutions into cohesive voicing families. The chapter establishes three source scales for quartal voicings over D half-diminished (Eb major, Db major, and F melodic minor), with Db major presenting a tricky transformation that reframes the chord as D7(#9) and invokes tritone substitution to justify mixolydian quartal voicings. Critical rules govern register and application: avoid muddy lower notes (remedied by dropping to 3-note voicings), restrict lydian dominant to unresolved dominant 7ths, and use mixolydian quartal voicings only over V chords resolving to major. The master's characteristic move is permitting non-family substitutions when voice-leading demands it, as when D#/E (F#7(13)b9) replaces Fm(maj7)add4. The pedagogical stance separates chord ideas from groove ideas, emphasizing that block chord examples should be memorized rather than merely analyzed, with Big Band listening and singing as the prescribed internalization technique.
